title: Testing APIs
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of testing apis and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn testing apis through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Testing APIs matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines testing apis as part of testing and code quality. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: JSON payloads; Authentication headers; API permissions; Pagination and filtering; Error responses. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: JSON payloads
items.text: JSON payloads crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Authentication headers
items.text: Authentication identifies a user; authorization determines what the user can do. Prefer Django’s built-in password/user/session machinery and test account recovery and anonymous access.

items.title: API permissions
items.text: Model permissions are a useful starting point but do not automatically enforce ownership of every individual record. Scope each lookup and mutation to the caller’s authorized objects.

items.title: Pagination and filtering
items.text: For Pagination and filtering, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Error responses
items.text: Treat Error responses as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

content_blocks.troubleshooting: Choose methods based on the operation’s semantics and use security headers consistent with the deployment policy.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “Testing APIs” and the related concept “JSON payloads”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to JSON payloads. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe testing apis, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a framework fragment without its imports, configuration, model, or URL context.
common_mistakes.why: The snippet may be incomplete when separated from a Django project.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the stated prerequisites and run the relevant management check or focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting input or relying only on a happy-path example.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid values, unauthorized requests, or concurrent activity can violate assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and add a negative or boundary test.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating the development sample as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Production hosting, secrets, storage, monitoring and resource limits differ from local use.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the current deployment/security references and document untested areas.
